title: Treatment of acne scars
what: Acne scars are pits and uneven spots on the skin. They can be made much less noticeable with lasers, peels, microneedling, and other methods.
why: When the pimples have cleared but pits and scars remain.
duration: one procedure usually takes 30 to 60 minutes; treatment is a course of several sessions
tell_doctor: Whether you have new pimples right now
Whether you take or have taken acne pills
If you have had cold sores (herpes) or thick raised scars (keloids)
Whether you have been in the sun recently

prepare.title: Pimples
prepare.text: Active pimples are treated first. Scars are treated once there are few new breakouts.

prepare.title: Sun
prepare.text: Do not sunbathe before the procedures.

prepare.title: Expectations
prepare.text: Scars usually get shallower but do not disappear completely. Ask your doctor what is realistic for you.

steps: The doctor examines the scars and chooses a method
Your skin is cleaned, and a numbing cream is usually applied
The procedure is done: laser, microneedling, peel, or another method
Your skin is cooled and a soothing product is applied
The date of your next session is set
feel: Warmth, tingling, sometimes a burning feeling
Afterward, redness and swelling for a few days
after: Use the products your doctor prescribed
Do not touch or pick at your skin
Results are easier to see after several sessions
red_flags: Blisters, pus, severe pain, or a fever: see a doctor
Dark patches appear: show them to your doctor

faq.a: They are usually made much less noticeable, but not always gone completely.

faq.q: Can scars be treated while I still have pimples?
faq.a: Usually the pimples are treated first. Your doctor will decide when to start.

reminders.text: Scar treatment tomorrow. Stay out of the sun, and come with a bare face, no makeup.
